summary: Long-lived low-CPU / high-GPU streams holding slots and causing reserved-pool throughput erosion
description:
Issue summary:
- Since ~2026-03-13T07:30UTC several reserved GPU pools serving Nimbus Analytics have shown a gradual p99/p95 throughput degradation over a 2–3 hour window. The symptom set is a slowly rising request queue, batch slot allocation increases despite constant request rate, and a corresponding step-up in tail latency.

Impact:
- Nimbus (dedicated tenant) reports degraded batch throughput and higher p99 latency; customer reports timeouts for multi-token streams and intermittent throttling. Business affected: nightly ingestion pipelines and interactive inference endpoints.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: us-east reserved cluster (pool-id: rp-us-east-12).
- Runtime version: serving-runtime v3.12.7.
- Scheduler: gang-scheduler v1.4.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1. Reproduce workload shape: many long-lived streaming requests (60–120s) that do heavy decode and minimal CPU preprocessing.
2. Start 200 concurrent small-batch streams (1–4 tokens per iteration) pinned to rwkv-13b-quant.
3. Observe scheduler's slot accounting and batcher metrics over 30–90 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- Certain streams keep GPU slot assignments for entire stream lifetime; slot release doesn't correlate to actual GPU utilization.
- Autoscaler does not trigger additional capacity because slot occupancy appears steady (but effective usable throughput is lower).
- KV-cache entries for these streams grow and cause collisions with small short-lived requests, increasing serialization in the batcher.

Expected behavior:
- Long-lived streams should let batching multiplex other requests without holding slots in a way that blocks normal batching. Autoscaler should detect real utilization drop/pressure and scale accordingly.

Temporary workaround applied:
- Support configured an eviction soft-threshold (5m) for long-held soft-locked slots for this pool and applied a conservative slot reclaim policy. This immediately recovered ~30% of throughput for the customer's critical route.
steps_to_reproduce: Start 200 concurrent streaming requests: 60–120s lifetime, minimal cpu per-step work, model rwkv-13b-quant
Monitor batcher slot-occupancy and scheduler assigned_slots metrics for rp-us-east-12 over 60 minutes
Compare kv-cache size and eviction_rate against a normal short-stream workload
comments: 2026-03-13T08:40Z - Aisha Kumar (Support): Customer opened with alerting showing p99 increase on two interactive routes. Initial triage shows pool rp-us-east-12. Marking as P1 due to ingestion SLAs.

2026-03-13T09:05Z - Benjamin Ortiz (SRE): Confirmed slow drift in throughput. Not seeing obvious GPU saturation; per-GPU util at 45–60% while queue grows. Suspect slot lock behavior from long-lived streams.

2026-03-13T10:12Z - Nimbus Analytics (Customer - Rachel Li): We started a new streaming job yesterday evening that keeps an open connection while polling for outputs. This roughly matches when the degradation began.

2026-03-13T11:00Z - Benjamin Ortiz (SRE): Applied temporary slot-reclaim soft-threshold (5m). Early effect: pending_queue reduced ~27% and p99 for customer's critical route improved from 2.4s -> 1.1s. Continuing investigation into root cause and autoscaler signals.

2026-03-14T09:20Z - Margo Chen (Infra): Found that scheduler heartbeat coalescing and slot bookkeeping path does not decrement 'logical_hold' when stream-only activity enters a steady-state decode loop. Raising a runtime bug: GH-2145.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Long-lived streams set a logical slot hold that doesn't get decremented unless explicit release path runs; decode-only steps don't trigger slot-update callbacks.
Hypothesis 2: KV-cache growth causes increased serialization inside batcher; small streams wait behind large held slots leading to effective throughput drop despite available GPU cycles.
Metric evidence: per-GPU util at <70% while assigned_slots >> active_batching_slots. This indicates slots are 'owned' but not enabling multiplexing.
Correlated config: rwkv-13b-quant runtime path uses a different kernel lifecycle and may bypass the usual slot-heartbeat. Reproducer confirms kernel path correlates to the issue.
Related prior tickets: linked SUP-271903 shows similar pocket of slot-lock but with ephemeral streams causing starvation; this incident differs because streams are long-lived and low-CPU.
Next investigative steps: instrument slot-heartbeat delta, add metric for 'logical_hold_duration' per stream, and run ablation with kernel path disabled for same workload.

Action items: SRE to add canary patch to reclaim logic; Runtime team to patch heartbeat callback (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2145) and add unit test for decode-only step path.
resolution: Mitigation in place: soft eviction/reclaim applied to rp-us-east-12; observed ~30% throughput recovery on customer routes. A runtime patch (PR 2145) submitted to fix heartbeat decrement on decode-only steps. Longer-term patches: (1) make autoscaler use effective_throughput metric (not just assigned_slots), (2) add kv-cache eviction tuning for long-lived streams. Plan: schedule controlled rollout of runtime fix in canary pools on 2026-03-17 then full pool rollout 2026-03-20.
follow_up_tasks: QA: Create automated test for long-lived decode-only stream slot release
Product: Expose 'long-lived stream' warning in Console for Dedicated pools
SRE: Monitor effective_throughput metric and create alert if assigned_slots > active_batching_slots by 25% for >15m
workaround_notes: Applied eviction soft-threshold (5m) to the pool which reclaims idle logical holds earlier than default. This is a stop-gap; it may impact very long-running customer sessions that intentionally hold slots (we coordinated with Nimbus).
customer_communication: 2026-03-13T12:15Z - Sent interim update to Nimbus support contact (Rachel Li) describing mitigation and next steps. Promised follow-up timeline for runtime patch and canary rollout. Customer acknowledged and requested notification on canary success before full rollout.
estimated_root_cause: Scheduler + runtime slot bookkeeping mismatch: decode-only long-lived streams were not decrementing logical_hold counters, so slots appeared occupied preventing batch multiplexing and confusing autoscaler signals.
notes_for_engineering: Runtime heartbeat callback needs a unit test covering decode-only step paths. Autoscaler should incorporate a derived throughput metric to avoid decisioning purely on assigned_slots. Consider kv-cache per-tenant caps for dedicated pools to avoid cross-tenant collision.
